findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks all custom grant-type factories
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is the extension point implemented by custom OAuth2 grant types, but getShortcut() was added as an abstract interface method with no default implementation. Every existing third-party factory therefore fails to compile/link against this version, and a factory that returns null at runtime will also fail startup when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory puts the null shortcut into a ConcurrentHashMap. Add a default method (for example returning the unknown shortcut) so existing providers continue to work.

findings.title: Public copy constructor of OAuth2GrantType.Context was removed
findings.body: The public Context(Context) copy constructor was deleted while the main constructor now also dereferences formParams to capture grantType. Code outside this PR (custom grant types or wrappers that cloned a Context before delegating) can no longer compile, and any caller constructing Context with a null formParams map now gets a NullPointerException from formParams.getFirst(...) instead of merely storing null. Restore/deprecate the copy constructor and handle a null formParams if that was previously tolerated.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong substring offsets
findings.body: The encoded prefix is 6 characters laid out as sessionType[0,2) tokenType[2,4) grantType[4,6), but the matcher checks substring(3,5) and returns false when that substring equals the expected grant shortcut. As written it accepts token IDs with any grant shortcut (substring(3,5) will normally not equal the expected value, so it falls through to the UUID check) and can reject a correct one, so expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken do not actually verify the new grant encoding and will mask missing/incorrect GRANT_TYPE wiring in the grants they cover. It should be: if (!items[0].substring(4,6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;

findings.title: Constructor validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
findings.body: Line 73 repeats Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and later produces a token ID ending in ':null' (or an NPE downstream) instead of failing fast at construction. Change the second check to requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...).

findings.title: encodeTokenId does not validate the 2-character shortcut length required by the decoder
findings.body: encodeTokenId concatenates session/token/grant shortcuts without checking that the grant shortcut is exactly 2 characters, while getTokenContextFromTokenId (line 74) rejects any prefix whose length is not exactly 6. A grant factory returning a 1- or 3-character shortcut (the new OAuth2GrantTypeFactory javadoc even says 'usually like 3-letters') will silently mint access tokens whose IDs can never be decoded, throwing IllegalArgumentException on later use. Validate shortcut length (and uniqueness) at encode/startup time and fix the javadoc to state the 2-character requirement.

findings.title: Token issuance now fails hard for any unregistered grant type instead of using the unknown fallback
findings.body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext maps a missing grant type to the UNKNOWN shortcut 'na', but encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException when a non-null grant string has no registered shortcut. Because TokenManager.initToken now runs this encoder for every access token, any flow that sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE to a value not backed by an OAuth2GrantTypeFactory id (legacy/custom token-endpoint grants or extensions that set the attribute themselves) changes from successfully issuing a token to failing the whole token request with a 500. Fall back to the UNKNOWN shortcut for unmapped grants instead of aborting issuance.
